ideas.pitch: A web-based interactive power system fault analysis and load flow simulator built for electrical engineering students to test contingency scenarios.
ideas.title: GridSim Live
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core electrical engineering fundamentals evaluated by MNNIT Allahabad's SMP assessment by offering a practical simulation tool that proves deep conceptual understanding of power flow and fault currents.

ideas.pitch: An online browser-based virtual laboratory simulator for testing speed-torque characteristics and armature reaction of DC machines.
ideas.title: MachineLab Virtual DC
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the winning pattern of a working live demo, translating complex theoretical equations of electrical machines into an instantly testable web simulator.

ideas.pitch: A quick-computation tool for control systems engineers to instantly derive transfer functions, stability margins, and root locus plots from network parameters.
ideas.problem_statement: Test concepts related to Control Systems.
ideas.title: BodePlotter Pro
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves a tedious mathematical pain point for electrical engineering students during rigorous technical assessments by providing immediate, visually verifiable feedback.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight browser-based circuit netlist parser and waveform visualizer tailored for transient analysis in power electronics converters.
ideas.title: PowerSpice Viewer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Emphasises Genuinely hard engineering by implementing a real-time numerical parsing engine for electrical circuits entirely within client-side code.

ideas.pitch: An algorithmic step-by-step solver for complex AC/DC circuits using Thevenin, Norton, and Maximum Power Transfer theorems with nodal analysis visualization.
ideas.problem_statement: Assess knowledge of Electrical Circuits and Network Theory.
ideas.title: NetworkTheorem Solver
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides exact academic utility for an engineering assessment event by double-checking student problem sets with clear intermediate node-voltage calculations.
